changes: Export the 22 recommended React syntax/scope rules through the native plugin, retaining the original five-rule central defaults; expose the original React profile separately with original options/severities.
Replace utility barrel imports with direct licensed standalone utility source and copied AST predicate helpers; retain semantics.
Omit ESLint config assembly and use native context.filename/sourceCode/getScope/getDeclaredVariables directly; no compatibility fallbacks or engine dependency.

Use native lexical import/render-result bindings when aggressive module reporting is off, preventing shadowed/import-unrelated names from being treated as Testing Library utilities. Preserve explicit aggressive-reporting options.

Two waitFor fixes remove exact AST statement ranges and use their source text instead of assuming standalone whole-line statements or an extra line past EOF; this preserves minified/single-line files and fix idempotence.
Remove seven unconfigured rule initializers; retain licensed shared helper code needed by the 22 exposed rules.

Native await-async-events/queries/utils and prefer-screen-queries accept an optional first-rule-options utilsModule string. Helpers read actual defaulted rule options and pass the module directly to genuine lexical import resolution; absent options preserve original global settings. This allows a narrow native override to recognize a project test-helper module without globally recognizing it in helper/e2e scopes. No override.settings, fabricated context, runner or checker service is used. Existing eventModule options and all other rules remain available.
User-event methods and setup instances follow native import and variable binding identities, preserving official/custom aliases and same-file setup wrappers while avoiding locally shadowed actors.
